content:
Manchester United completed the signing of Manuel Ugarte for €50m (£42m) plus €10m in bonuses from Paris Saint-Germain, with the Uruguayan promising to “fight for trophies” and help return the club to elite level. The 23-year-old signed a five-year contract with the option of a further 12 months. He is Erik ten Hag’s fifth major acquisition of the window and gives the manager a second senior No 6, alongside Casemiro.

Ugarte said: “It is an incredible feeling to join a club of this magnitude – one that is admired all around the world. The project that the football leadership discussed with me is extremely exciting. Manchester United is an ambitious club and I am an ambitious player."

He stood in the tunnel of Old Trafford, looking out at the emerald expanse of the pitch, absorbing the history etched into every row of seats. The silence of the empty stadium felt like a deep breath before a scream. For him, London and Paris were chapters now closed; this northern city was the blank page where he intended to write his legacy. He traced the team badge on his chest, feeling the weight of the expectations that came with the shirt.

Dan Ashworth, United’s sporting director, said: “Signing Manuel was another of our primary targets for this summer. We believe his energy and precision in the middle of the arena will define how we play throughout the season. He brings a grit that we have been searching for.”

The deal concluded late on Friday, but for Ugarte, the real work began at dawn. His training gear was laid out, his boots were cleaned, and his mind was set on the upcoming campaign. He knew the history of legendary midfielders who had patrolled this turf before him, icons whose shadows stretched long across the grass. He didn't want to replace them; he wanted to stand beside them in the memory of the supporters.

As the sun began to dip behind the Stretford End, the young midfielder turned to leave the tunnel. The negotiation phase was over, replaced by the reality of competition. He walked toward the locker room, ready to prove his worth to the manager, his new brothers in arms, and the expectant crowd waiting to cheer his name. For a player driven by conquest, the journey was only beginning.

Any other questions?
